findings.summary: Paint all label guides before all label text. The current per-label guide/text pairs let a later guide overpaint an earlier name and its protective outline. In the added crowded drawing fixture, Courier is at (300,134), WWWW is at (300,100), and the later WWWW guide runs from (300,150) to (300,104), directly through Courier. Separate guide and text passes make the intended layer order explicit for both bodies and marks.

Fresh round-1 design review of the entire target change set from 55b59c9133056c1d6471274a9676a7d5649196ac to frozen tree be84c53c033bbfcb3977e8933f87ba9531405b7d. The candidate includes tracked and previously untracked files: 101 paths, 99 text files and two binary catalog baselines. I verified every one of the 101 frozen blob SHA-256 values against round-1-candidate.json; there were no mismatches. Launchpad context is the declared tree 7652b07a842cecabfa55fc4142f842733ab64758 against a5e7076cfe1082d888966223f544e17d471324ae. Only the scratch report was written.

One should-fix design finding, DI-01. This follows statically from SVG document order and the exact coordinates selected by motionLabels for the existing new crowded fixture, without introducing a new adversarial test. The first Courier label uses the preferred y=134. WWWW cannot share that box, so the nearest clear row is y=100. Its guide is emitted after Courier text and crosses that text at x=300. CSS paint-order applies inside an element; it cannot keep an earlier text outline above a subsequently painted line. A guide layer followed by a text layer addresses both body/body and body/mark ordering without changing physical positions, placement policy, or any model.

The main design choice is sound: one pure drawing-level placement helper removes forty models from responsibility for fitting names to viewport fonts, retains independent physical anchors, and keeps the renderer API small. The twenty new models follow the existing per-study pure-function pattern, using exported calculation/state helpers rather than coupling models to one another. The detailed computational reads included finite-wall intersections and clearance, Corner trap, coordinated formation movement, collision prediction, iterative flight search and its explicit terminal statuses, the jump phase machine, ballistic roots and exact event times, local 3D projection, velocity matching, direct kinematic samples, seeded wander, actuator and motor integration. State-to-presentation preparation and dependency/test structures were inspected across all twenty models and their specs. No further concrete design change earned a finding.

The executable-model disclosure remains in the explanation component and receives a compact mapped view shape. The chart legend is selected in the mapper, preserving the drawing components as readers of declarative models. I checked the existing facade error isolation: a model exception fails its study and leaves the surrounding reading available. The fifteen first-batch spec edits preserve their physical-coordinate checks while moving name measurements to labelX. The registry, records, summary and tooling/browser test edits were included in the path/structure review; producer/consumer consistency and criterion judgments remain with their assigned workers.

Coverage limits: this was a bounded static design review, with detailed reading concentrated on changed shared code and model computations; long authored prose and repeated numerical assertions were inspected through structured summaries and selected excerpts rather than independently re-proving every claim. The two binary visual baselines were hash-identified but not visually inspected. I ran no test suite, gate, browser, model sweep, background task or agent. The parent's retained preflight and glyph-sweep results are context, not my executable validation. I did not review private/local records or intake, did not reuse an earlier reviewer's report, and make no criterion verdict. DI-01 is a layering finding, outside the sweep's label-versus-label metric.
